entries.text: Special Sitting

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Convened via Kenya Gazette Notice No.10309 of 9th December, 2020)

entries.label: other
entries.text: The House met at the Senate Chamber, Parliament Buildings, at 9.00 a.m.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: [The Speaker (Hon. Lusaka) in the Chair]

entries.label: other
entries.text: PRAYER

entries.label: heading
entries.text: PRAYER

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Hon. Senators, today is a continuation of yesterday. I see one party has come in. So, let us wait for a few minutes for the other party to come in so that we proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have seen two of the legal representatives. I thought we could do something internal about the process et cetera so that all of us are clear before all of them come in and have more Members in the House.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel for the Governor, give us a few minutes we do some housekeeping then you can come in.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you, very much.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I request that you allow us to do a closed door session for about 20 minutes. The parties can wait outside together with the ones who will sit in the---

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud Consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Use the microphone behind you. Is that better?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: .: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am applying that we have a closed door session for about 20 minutes, we do preliminary issues and allow the parties to stay outside so that we can discuss our internal matters then they come in.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is granted and in order. We are in a closed session until 9.25 a.m. So, no cameras. Senators can now raise their internal issues.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (All members of the public and the media withdrew from the galleries)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The House went into camera)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The House adjourned temporarily at 9.10 a.m.)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The House resumed at 9.30 a.m.)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Hon. Senators, if you may take your seats, we want to proceed. Hon. Senators and the parties, we are back to our open session. We had a brief in- house session to sort out our own things. In order to clarify a few things, the programme today will start at 9.30 a.m. There will be evidence by the Governor, evidence of witnesses, if any, cross-examination and re-examination. All that has been allocated four hours and you should be able to tell us how you want to manage that time, including the cross-examination from the other side, so that we do not run into the problems that we had yesterday. I will be giving you an opportunity to tell us how you want us to manage it. At 1.30 p.m., we will have questions, requests and clarifications from the Senators after which we will have a lunch break. Between 2.30 p.m. to 3.30 p.m. we will have 60 minutes closing statements on behalf of the County Assembly. From 3.30 p.m. to 4.30 p.m. we will have 60 minutes closing statements on behalf of the Governor. Between 4.30 p.m. and 6.30 p.m. we shall have a closed session. The court will retreat to look at all that has been presented. We hope that by 6.30 p.m. we should be able to take the vote. Counsel for the Governor, you are welcome. Start by telling us how you want us to manage the four hours.

entries.label: heading
entries.text: GOVERNOR OF NAIROBI CITY COUNTY

entries.label: heading
entries.text: PRESENTATION OF THE CASE OF THE NAIROBI CITY COUNTY GOVERNOR

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Good morning, Mr. Speaker, Sir and hon. Senators. Thank you very much for this occasion and giving us an opportunity to testify. On behalf of His Excellency the Governor, we will be calling out witnesses to rebut the allegations leveled against him. We will also have the Governor himself testify in order to dispel the notion that he is guilty of the allegations leveled against him. We will be using the affidavits in support. My first witness is the Hon. Sylvia Museiya. I wish to have her in the dock. I will be within the time that has been prescribed. I presume that you have given us from 9.35 a.m., so then we should finish within the four hours.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: How will you apportion the four hours because you must also accommodate the other side, so that you do not take three and half hours and then they are left with 30 minutes?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we will be fair enough. However, the---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Masika Wetangula
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. You have rightly directed that time management is critical. It will be absolutely helpful for the learned lawyer, Mr. Kinyanjui, to tell you and the House, how many witnesses he is calling so that you sequence how they are going to be called, the time he spends examining them, the time you allow cross-examination and re-examination, if any, so that we can have a more orderly and time-bound process. We do not want a situation where he calls one witness, moves on for three hours and then says that: "I have three others and I have only one hour, I need more time."

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Precisely; that is what I was saying. We need to be very clear from the beginning so that we manage our time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir and Hon. Wetangula. Thank you for the concern. I intend to take a minimum of about five to 10 minutes on every witness. However, for the Governor, on account of the extended accusations that have been leveled against him, I will take the chunk of the time that is going to be outstanding.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: How many other witnesses do you have?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In sum, I have seven witnesses. My first witness is Hon. Sylvia Museiya.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay, Counsel for the County Assembly, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Sorry, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I had addressed you so that we cover the ground and do not come back to it yesterday. The issue had arisen as to the document that I had filed in consequence of the late service of the documents by the County Assembly. Immediately upon the delivery of your Ruling, pursuant to Rule 29 of the Fifth Schedule, Part I of the Standing Orders, I pleaded and sought for the leave of this House for the admission of the Governor's evidence and it was so admitted. However, you directed that you would confirm with the HANSARD that, indeed, that was it. I referenced the document when I was cross-examining the chief witness No.1 for the County Assembly. It was submitted and I was given by the Clerk's office the designation as No.10H and 10G, that those were the designations in consequence of your said Ruling.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. We are ready to proceed with today's proceedings, but we seem to be constrained of the disclosure from the Governor's side in so far as the question of the witnesses that are being called are in issue. When you gave us your directions prior to the commencement of these proceedings, it was clear that the proceedings will be guided by Rule 7 of this House. Most importantly, in the question of the disclosure of the witnesses that the parties are intending to rely with, that has not been done to us. Mr. Kinyanjui is always very fast to cling to the provisions of Article 50 about fair hearing and also abrogates the same when it comes to the part of the prosecutor. Mr. Speaker, Sir, the statements that Mr. Kinyanjui is now calling the witnesses to rely on have not been furnished. That is why we probably got into this issue. The document that Mr. Kinyanjui is seeking leave to address us on was not part of the document that was served. That will be a very serious miscarriage of justice if we are to prosecute or defend a case that has not been laid bare in advance. Despite how able advocates might be, despite the team of advocates that one might have, if evidence has not been laid bare in advance, the prosecutor will have serious uphill in rebutting the prepositions that will be mentioned. Allow me to ask Mr. Kokebe just to have a highlight on that issue.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Yes, Counsel for the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. With tremendous respect, I beg to differ with my learned friend. The affidavits of all my witnesses have been filed and served, including that of His Excellency the Governor. The document of my first witness is contained in Volume Three of (d). This is termed; Filed on the 15th of December, 2020 at 3.45 p.m., duly served on the County Assembly advocates. Volume Three, on page 654 is there and was duly served. That is my first witness. My second witness is also there. I have the affidavits annexed and they are in Volume Two, also served on the 15th of December, 2020 at 3.45 p.m. It is running from 200 to 278. We have that evidence and it was duly served. I think that the objection should be overruled so that I can proceed without any further ado. The lamentation is totally, with respect, misplaced. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Hon. Senators and Counsel, we want to be fair to everyone. Therefore, for this court to be able to come up with a fair judgment I want us to go into a closed session for another 20 minutes then I call you back.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Much obliged.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Sen. Mutula Kilonzo, Jnr.
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. For good order, the lawyers are referring to documents and we have different references. For example, the Volume Three that my learned friend, Mr. Kinyanjui is referring to is 10D(2). So, for good measure, when we come back, I propose that they use the references that we have. Otherwise, we are getting lost in the volume twos and threes. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: When we come back, let us use the references that we have. The Secretariat can also assist us to check the documents that they are referring to. Let us come back after 20 minutes.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The House temporarily adjourned at 9.45 a.m.)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The House resumed at 10.20 a.m.)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Take your seats; I am on my feet. Unless you want to freeze.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Hon. Senators took their seats)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Welcome back to our open session. Before we went into a closed session, there was an issue we were dealing with which has been determined by the Senate. That was the admission of seven witnesses. This is what I want to draw the Counsel to; what has informed the decision of the Senate that I will be communicating shortly. That is the Fifth Schedule, Rule No.6 which states- "Where the Governor chooses to appear before the Senate, the Governor shall be required, within three days of the invitation under Rule 4(a), on a date specified in the invitation, to file an answer to the charges with the Office of the Clerk of the Senate, in which the Governor shall set out- a) the Governor's response to the particulars of the allegations; b) how the Governor proposes to appear before the Senate; whether in person, by advocate or in person and by advocate; c) the names and addresses of the persons to be called as witnesses, if any, and a statement by each such witnesses; and, d) any other evidence to be relied upon." From our records, we have no statements from any witnesses by the Governor. We also do not have names provided at the time they were supposed to be provided for the witnesses to be examined here. Therefore, the Senate, having looked at that and considered that yesterday, as the Speaker and the Senate, allowed some materials to be brought in. Out of the scheduled time, the Senate has ruled that only the Governor will be heard, but the other witnesses will not be heard based on Rule No.6 of the Fifth Schedule. It is so directed. So, proceed and let us know how you want to use your four hours that start now.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I did attach the affidavit of Hon. Sylvia Museiya. It was also part of the originally filed bundle. I also filed the affidavit of Mr. Emmanuel Kenga as part of the original bundle. It is, in fact, headed---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: We wanted the list of names and addresses of the persons to be called as witnesses, if any, and statements by each such witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, a pdf list was sent by e-mail to the Clerk. I conferred with the Clerk yesterday and they confirmed. In fact, even this morning, I did. I also sent a copy to the Clerk of the Nairobi City County Assembly. At page 654 Volume Three, you will find the statement of the first witness I intend to call.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Is it the document that we have?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, yes. This is originally filed and served. It is not introduced in any way. I also confirmed with the Office of the Clerk that it is, in fact, headed: "Opposing Affidavit on Behalf of H. E the Governor as a Witness". The list was provided as well. So, I am a bit baffled---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Where is the list? Just a minute.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the list was served on pdf. This is Volume Three on page 654.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Mr. Kinyanjui showed the Speaker a document)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Clerks-at-the-Table consulted the Speaker)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you will also notice in Volume Three page 528, my other witness also swore a statement. It was equally served in the original document and it is not a late admission.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order! Yes, Counsel, what is it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with your kind permission, let me finish.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay, I will give you an opportunity.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City Governor)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I just want to point out salient issues pursuant to your ruling which was very Solomonic.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Let us consult in low tones. I need to hear what is being said.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the documents that you have been referred to were produced as affidavits in Petition No.35. They were not intended to be in these particular proceedings. These are in a Petition to which the court has already heard and dismissed the same. Is this Senate going to sit as an appellate court? I doubt so. That is to the effect of the various affidavits that you have been referred to. Fundamentally, when parties appeared herein on 15th between 3.40 p.m. to 3.45 p.m. there was a Senate inventory that was produced. In that inventory, that particular document was marked 10F. That was the last document that was produced. Documents 10G and 10H are new. They are strange to us. Mr. Speaker, Sir, this is a House of records. Following the Waititu decision, if you do not produce those particular documents, why then should you call this House to give you redress? If this House will be called upon to abrogate on its rules of procedure, what precedence is this House being asked to make? We plead with you and the hon. Members that documents that were brought outside that particular timeframe be locked out. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I remember when we appeared here, Dr. Okello advised that even if it was a holding document, let it be filed. These two documents that are now being brought to us were not even produced as holding documents. For that reason, we plead that you follow the precedent that this House has set before. If you allow me, just before I yield to my learned senior, Mr. Kinyanjui, I was dealing with this with my friend Mr. Okatch. I might have just missed something, but just so that it is clear for the House.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Proceed, Mr. Okatch.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, thank you for the opportunity. There is only one germane issue that you ought to consider. Your Rules are very clear, that you have to provide the addresses and names of the persons who are to be called as witnesses in advance. It is not only for our sake, but for the sake of this House and for planning purposes. It is for the Members of this honorable House to know in advance the nature of evidence that you will be calling in your defense. We complied with that and notified them in advance. Mr. Speaker, Sir, today, we have affidavits which have not been indicated as witness affidavits. They are just affidavits. Some of them, as we have been told, were filed in an ongoing case in court. This is such that even ourselves, looking at them, they were just mere attachments that maybe the Governor who has filed an affidavit would have referred to. It will be utterly unfair, not only to us, but even to this House, for these particular affidavits to be introduced and for these particular people to be taken as witnesses against your rules of procedure. Let everyone be bound by that. If this is what they chose, let them lie on the bed that they actually created.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Orengo, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Minority Leader)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, although you have ruled on this matter, I know the counsel from both sides would ask themselves the question why this particular Rule No. 6 is there in the Standing Orders, and I can glean to. First, it is because we are time bound. All the information has to reach the Senate before the trial starts. You cannot be making a case in the middle of the case. Secondly, it is to ensure that no side is ambushed. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I truly plead that what we should do now is substantial justice as opposed to being enslaved with technicalities. That is the spirit of Article 159 of the Constitution, which applies to judicial institutions. I have just seen some of the affidavits. Like on this volume, I think it is Volume 3D (2) on Page 648. There is an affidavit of Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach. Prior to that, on Page 644, this is in relation to a certificate of photographic, print and video evidence. Mr. Speaker, Sir, the point I want to make is that if the witness that they intend to call, the affidavit is found in this volume, and if this volume was filed on time, in order to be seen to be fair and that justice is not only done but is seen to be done, there is no harm in allowing them to call the witnesses whose affidavits were filed on time. Just in answer to the advocate to the County Assembly, the affidavit that is found on Page 648 gives the name of the deponent, his occupation and address in Nairobi. There is a jurat at the end of the affidavit. It was sworn on 13th December, 2020. The heading has nothing to do with any court. It is in relation to these proceedings. Mr. Speaker, Sir, my position would be that just because they did not provide a list, that should not be used against the Governor because we want to render substantial justice. The other side would not be ambushed because their affidavit is in this volume and they have been served. In those circumstances, I pray without further delay that if there is an affidavit that was filed on time, those witnesses should be allowed to give evidence. If the counsel from the County Assembly wanted a little time to look at the specific affidavits, they should not be allowed to call anybody. They should say: "We are calling this witness because he swore an affidavit. The affidavit is found on this page and is sworn on this date and only strictly to those persons who have affidavits in these volumes." Mr. Speaker, Sir, I pray.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I will only allow two interventions by Sen. Linturi and Sen. Mutula Kilonzo Jnr. then we proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Franklin Mithika Linturi
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Briefly let me add to what senior counsel Sen. Orengo has just alluded to. We cannot run away from looking at the effect of that decision that has been made. The reason is because the decision has the effect of trying or infringing on or violating the rights of the Governor to defend himself in such a serious matter. When we do not admit his witnesses and when it has been proved that there are such affidavits that were filed on time and then denying that opportunity, I think in terms of even how things or matters would be conducted in future, the decision we are taking would have some bearing on how we conduct ourselves in future. Mr. Speaker, Sir, let us also remember that we are trying to develop precedence and jurisprudence on how impeachments should be conducted because this is a very new phenomenon. In advancing this matter and considering all the issues that have been raised, I do not think anybody will suffer any serious prejudice if there is admission of the evidence of the affidavits that were filed on time. We should really give that opportunity. As a House, we are not strictly bound by the strict rules of evidence that we cannot accommodate. That is why I think the Standing Orders give you some bit of latitude. I would request you to apply your discretion considering the matter before this House is weighty. We really need to be seen to be very fair in this matter.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Finally, Sen. Mutula Kilonzo Jnr., then I give direction.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I believe you agreed that we will make this very short, so that we do not appear to be taking positions about the parties. The sentiments by Sen. Orengo are correct. If these documents were brought in, in advance, we cannot, therefore, turn a blind ear to them. This is because they are already here. The only folly is that, normally Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui is very organized, but he must admit to us that in this case, he was not. This is because at the top of the documents, he has written affidavit for governor, but in the middle, he has attached other documents. Mr. Speaker, Sir, lastly for the other witnesses, and for our own purposes, Mr. Kinyanjui should indicate witness number one on page 654, witness number two on page 648, witness number three on page 700. He also owes us a duty as we sit here to be organized. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Susan Kihika will be the final one. Time is not on our side.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Susan Wakarura Kihika
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will be very brief. I also agree with my colleagues that given the fact that the affidavit had been filed on time, balancing that with the issue that the opposing counsel would have, in the sense that they would not know who the witnesses would be, they will not be prepared to either cross-examine them or be aware of what they would be coming in here to say. With the affidavits filed on time, then we can say that, that would not be a big issue. In the interest of justice, and given the very serious case that the governor is facing, I believe that we should allow the affidavits and the witnesses to come in as evidence. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Minority Leader)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, for you to exercise your discretion and for a matter of record, I think the counsels for the governor, Mr. Kinyanjui in particular, should admit that he did not comply with Rule 6 before you can proceed to exercise your discretion. Otherwise, if he insists that everything has been done in an orderly fashion, how would you be exercising your direction if there is no admission of non-compliance? For purposes of record, the advocate for the governor must say there has been no compliance. This is important because the Clerk has read a letter that was submitted to them which quoted verbatim, Rule 6 and gave the date and time. I think these matters may not end here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I appreciate the input and the very positive response from the hon. Members. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I do apologize for that. I do note that the request for the governor to comply with Rule 6 was submitted. Indeed, we attempted and made every effort to comply. However, the issue of the list of the witnesses may have arisen in complication because we named 57 Members of County Assembly (MCAs). My learned friend for the county government may have to proceed. We are calling all the 57 MCAs. We sent that in PDF form by email. I apologize about not listing pages to be the focus of that specific witness. However, in all of the witness statements that we have filed, I will call only four, so that I do not disabuse them of the notion that we will call 57 MCAs. It is just those that have actually sworn the witness statements. These were served on time. I thank you. I, therefore, ask, urge and plead, that your discretion be exercised so that we can proceed. What has been served any assessments can be admitted.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, if you may, I do not want to prolong this issue. I want to make it clear that as the advocates appearing for the County Assembly, we have no issues with documents labelled as 10A to 10F. Our bone of contention for purposes of clarity and guiding you as and when you go to issue your discretion is 10G and 10H. Mr. Speaker, Sir, your discretion is a constitutional discretion because it shall be based on the context of the Standing Orders before you, which by virtue of Article 124 enjoy the presumption of constitutionality. The right that Mr. Kinyanjui is seeking for his client under Article 50 is the same that our clients are craving for. Mr. Speaker, Sir, in your discretion, kindly, consider the question of fair hearing and fair trial and the indolence of a party who fails to comply with the rules. Rules are made to be complied with, not for breach and not for mercy.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Hon. Senators and Counsel, we have to make progress. Having listened to all the parties and having looked at the documentation that is before us and using my discretion just the way I used my discretion yesterday to stretch the time, I will allow the four witnesses and the governor to appear. You will now have to tell me how you want to manage the time. How much time each witness is going to take.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I will take about five to 10 minutes on each of the four witnesses. Probably if they extend in terms of re-examination, 15 minutes factoring the cross-examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Fifteen minutes will be maximum.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I hope so, with tremendous respect.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Do not hope so. We have to agree so that we manage our time. Your four hours starts now. Proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: My fifth witness is His Excellency the Governor. Mr. Speaker, Sir, before I commence, my learned friend has said that he will not address documents H and I because they were a subject of your ruling yesterday. It was admitted and it is allowed. Thank you. My first witness is Hon. Silvia Museiya. Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Members, hon. Silvia Museiya has a deposition in volume three at page 654 running to the end of the document at page 657.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Witness for Nairobi City County Governor, (Hon. Silvia Museiya) took the oath)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Silvia Museiya, you saw a deposition in these proceedings before this Hon. Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I did.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is found in Volume III of document D at page 654 to page 657.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I did.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You are an Hon. Member of the Nairobi City County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I am.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You are aware that His Excellency the governor is facing impeachment proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I am.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In relation to the said impeachment proceedings before the County Assembly, what do you have to say about the said process?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I will say that the impeachment process was procured largely by duress and coercion; not so much because of the substance of the impeachment, but the interests of some individuals, especially the leadership of the House. I will explain this in three ways. One, there was a disciplinary action commenced against me and three others at the Jubilee Party three days to impeachment, which ended up at around 6.30 p.m., and there was a decision by the disciplinary committee in a matter of two hours. That decision was later rescinded and stamped fake. However, two days to the impeachment, on Thursday, there was a communication from the chair, who is the Speaker, suspending three of us from being members of the Jubilee Party for three months and de-whipping us from our committees for six months. Secondly, there was a de-whipping of Hon. Mark Ndung'u from being the board member representing the Jubilee members. Thirdly, on the material day of the impeachment, 3rd December 2020, the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) Party sent a letter that was signed by Mr. Sifuna, who is the Secretary General of the Party, fining at least eight members between Kshs500,000 to Kshs1 million for disciplinary actions that had been commenced earlier. There was a letter purporting to de-whip Hon. Beatrice Waithera and Hon. Ruth Ndumi, both Members of the Jubilee Party because they were not paying party subscription fees. Therefore, all these go towards intimidation of members and alleged party position that the whip denied on public television. There was threatening. As members, we met to discuss and deliberate on the impeachment at Riverside. Thereafter, we were teargassed by the police, and they followed us to Upper Hill, which is the private residence of the Governor, from which we decided to go to Kwale and follow the proceedings from there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: How many were you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: We were about 67 at Riverside. However, at the time we arrived at Upper Hill, due to teargassing and all other issues, we were about 60. Fifty seven of us proceeded to Kwale, and we switched off our phones because they were ringing non-stop. The House leadership purported that there was a party position from His Excellency the President and former Prime Minister, Hon. Raila Odinga, saying that they had sanctioned the impeachment. We have the messages. Finally, I will speak on the issue of the leadership of the House. The impeachment that has been commenced is of the interest of a few people who hold leadership positions, not so much because of the substance of the impeachment, but because of their selfish interest. They say that it is either their way or you get out of the way. We have been victims of their abuse of office. The Governor is becoming a victim because if he does not do as they wish, they commence impeachment. Most of these Members in the leadership, from Hon. Guyo Abdi, who is the Leader of Majority and Hon. Ogada, who is the mover of the Motion, without prejudice to who they were, were former councillors. They have alleged that they have a way of running City Hall, and the Governor is interfering with their methodology of doing things. Therefore, this impeachment is not on substance, but because of the interest of a few people. They have used all means of intimidation of Members to procure this impeachment to this stage.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In Paragraph 4 of your affidavit, you say that there was no lawful virtual casting of votes during the purported voting on 3rd December. Why do you say that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: It is because of the Standing Orders of the Assembly, like those of the Senate, provide for two ways of voting. One is physical voting and the second one is electronic voting, where we put our cards and vote 'Yes' or 'No,' and it goes to the screen, where you can see that Hon. Silvia has voted 'No,' and another Member has voted 'Yes.' That did not happen.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In Volume 2 on page 301, is your image there as the people--- There were images of people at Kwale. Do you confirm that yours is No.17?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I am No.17 in the images out of the 57 of us who were physically in Kwale.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What do you have to say in terms of what you said in Paragraph 7 of your affidavit? In your affidavit, you say about the resolution that this Senate is dealing with.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I submit that there was no resolution of two-thirds of the Members to impeach the Governor of Nairobi. They did not have the number during the impeachment notice and at the Motion on 3rd December, which was on Thursday.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In Paragraph 9, you also allude to the logging into the Zoom facility.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I have to say that on Tuesday, when a communication from the chair purporting to remove or suspend us from the Jubilee Party was done, I did not log in, but my name was logged in. That has happened even before during the budget, where one person logins once, twice, thrice or four times. I remember when we passed the budget, we had a total of 138 people in the Zoom platform against 121 Members of the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, there were actually no 88 people? Mr. Okumu stood there and said that the threshold had been met. From your own testimony, was the threshold met?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: No, there was no threshold met.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So that I close, the issue of the payment by the county by the Governor, Hon. Okumu said that garbage collectors and only lawyers have been paid. In Paragraph 12, you refute that allegation.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I am the Chairperson of the Committee on Education. I moved a motion on payment and outsourcing of lawyers. I remember. I got information from the executive wing, which I have is part of the evidence, on payment of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) about 287, between Kshs1 million to Kshs2 million and another 115 between Kshs5 million to Kshs10 million. It is my submission that the County Government of Nairobi and Governor of Nairobi have done substantive effort in paying off some of the SMEs against the notion of lawyers. At the point where we have to pay lawyers, we actually must pay them because they even sue us to ensure that we pay. Therefore, we have to enforce court orders if given.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Yes, a clip was played earlier on here. If I could show her that so that she affirms and confirms that she was indeed at Kwale on that day. This is exhibit GM14 referenced at Page 112, Volume 1 at paragraph 69. While you were at Kwale, there was a concurrent meeting at the Nairobi City County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, there was. From the beginning, during the debate and up to the voting.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: It is alleged that some of you voted while at Kwale.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I can confirm that I did not vote. I can confirm that the people around me did not vote. We have a number of them within the precincts of the Senate. We did not vote. We did not even have the phones to vote.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So that we can have the clip played for you, I want us to confirm that indeed, you were at Kwale on the material day and the 57 of you at least never actually voted. I have referenced it at Page 69 of the Governor's affidavit.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Would you confirm that, that is the event that you speak of during the occasion of the impeachment proceedings at the County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Would you confirm that, indeed, at the County Assembly you were not able to access the data of the people voting?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: No, we could not access the data.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much. You will be asked questions on cross-examination. Please, be faithful to answer and be as brief as possible.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Switch off the video.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Hon. Silvia, good morning?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Good morning.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I did not want to interject when the Hon. Member was giving a statement from the understanding we had from the House yesterday. You started by saying that you were intimidated by way of suspension, de- whipping and on the material day of impeachment some Members of the ODM Party were de-whipped. Lastly, that there was a de-whipping of Waithera. Is it true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I did not mention Waithera. I mentioned Mark Ndung'u who was a County Assembly Board Member.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Is that material contained in your affidavit? The aspect of suspension, de-whipping and members of ODM being fined?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: It is in paragraph three. I have just gone to the lengths of expounding and explaining it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Can you read the specific part in that paragraph that talks about you being threatened and you even said you were teargassed in Upperhill before you went to Kwale?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Riverside then Upperhill.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Is that evidence in your affidavit?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: The evidence is not in my affidavit.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I wanted to bring that as a preliminary issue because I did not want to interject the Hon. Member as she was on her feet. Hon. Museiya, for how long have you been a Member of County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Since 2017.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. So, you are aware of Standing Order No.3 of the Nairobi City County Assembly Standing Orders?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: If you could read it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Standing Order No.3 talks about the Mace of the Assembly. Are you aware of that Standing Order?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I am.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Are you aware that where the Mace of the Assembly is, that is where the Assembly sits?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I am aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: The impeachment Motion was moved on the 3rd day of December where the Mace was. True or not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: True.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Did you get a communication from the Office of the Speaker for this specific day, the third day of December 2020?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I cannot confirm if I did or not because our phones were off.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Is it the fault of the Speaker that your phone was off?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I alluded earlier---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Give me a 'yes' or a 'no,' please.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: No, it was not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. Do you confirm that as a Member of the County Assembly, it is your responsibility to oversight, represent and legislate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: It is.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: And that whatever was happening on the 3rd day of December, 2020 was speaking to one of your roles; that is, the oversight role?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Right.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. You have brought evidence, alluded or testified that as at the time when the Motion was moved on 3rd December, 2020, you had been suspended.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I have.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: So, you did not have the capacity to participate in that process?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I agree.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Therefore, you cannot be a complainant to complain that you did participate in the process?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I can be because it is one of the issues I am raising on intimidation of Members. Reducing the number of people who could vote for the Governor or against the impeachment because we are perceived to be 'pro- Governor' which is a statement of fact.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Listen to my question. Can you participate in the affairs of the House while on suspension?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I cannot.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Let us say for argument's sake that you were. On this particular day, you decided voluntarily and deliberately to take yourself to a place that was outside Nairobi. Was it voluntary?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I had not volunteered to be included in Tuesday session.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Answer my question. You have said you were in Kwale.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I have said I was in Kwale.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You took yourself there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I did.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Can we go through Standing Order No.28 which talks about, 'regular sessions of the county assembly'. Are you aware of that Standing Order?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I am.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I want to specifically bring to your attention that it is required of you to be in the Assembly when required. Any MCA is supposed to be there when required. Is it true or not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: True.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: On this particular day, without leave of the Speaker you decided to be outside the jurisdiction of where you are supposed to be performing your duties. True or not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: The same Standing Order provides that we cannot miss the session eight times consecutively which I have not. I was in the House the week before. It is regular practice for Members not to participate in all House sessions. Refusing to vote is part of my right. That is what we were practicing in Kwale. We abstained from that vote.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: So, you did not participate deliberately?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: We did not participate deliberately.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. This will be my last question. I refer you to the County Assembly Powers and Privileges Act. Are you aware of this Act?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I am. I have been a Member of the Powers and Privileges Committee. Are you aware of Section 28 of the Powers and Privileges Act? If you could be kind to read it for me.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I will be so kind. Section 28 (1) says- "A person shall not by fraud, intimidation, force, insult or threat of any kind or by the offer or promise of any inducement or benefit of any kind, or by any other improper means- (a) Influence a Member in the performance of the Member's function as a Member. (b) Induce a Member to be absent from a County Assembly or a Committee at a particular time. (c) Attempt to compel a Member to declare himself or herself in favour or against a matter pending before or proposed or expected to be submitted to a County Assembly. "(2) A member shall not solicit, receive or accept any fee, compensation, gift, reward, favour or benefit of the kind for the member for another person in respect of- (a) Voting in any particular manner or not voting on a matter before the county assembly; (b) Promoting or opposing anything pending before or proposed or expected to be submitted to a county assembly; (c) Making a presentation to a county assembly; (3) A person who contravenes this Section commits and offence"

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: I am aware of it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You are aware of that particular section?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Very.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: A video has been played in which it has been exhibited and you have testified that you were not the only person in Kwale. There was not only two of you, but there was a number. Is it true or not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: True.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: When you went there, you were in the company, or you had the blessings of the Governor? Is it true or not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Not true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: It is not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Not true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: So, who took you to Kwale?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: We decided to take ourselves.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You took yourselves to Kwale?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, we did.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: What you are saying is that you were not influenced?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: No, I was not. Not at all.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You were not compelled?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: No, I was not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: So, you took yourself to Kwale and came back?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: Yes, I did.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Very well. That shall be all for this witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much. Just two questions on the re-examination. You were asked about your suspension and that you actually took no active part in the county assembly matters. What do you have to say about that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Silvia Museiya
entries.text: As Senators, you know the level of intimidation that can happen when people want to force a decision. We were mere victims by way of suspension and de-whipping, and we urge that the Senate, in its mandate of protecting devolution, that it shall protect its members towards taking an active democratic and transparent process. This is because the de-whipping had nothing to do with our conduct. As I said, I am an hon. Member, the Chair of the Committee on Education, and an active participant of the House. I think I have contributed most Motions, Statements, and even two Bills before the House. Therefore, there was no reason for me to be suspended other than to make a statement about the impeachment. It was supposed to cow us, especially nominated Members, so that we vote towards a certain direction. That message was communicated clearly and Members became very fearful. Finally, as I said, this impeachment is not on the substance of the Motion. It is on the interests of the leadership of the House led by the Count Assembly Minority Leader, Hon. Michael Ogada, the Mover of the Motion. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Museiya. I wish to have you rest, unless the hon. Senators--- Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have my second witness, Mr. Emanuel Kenga.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kenneth Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order! There is some intervention.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with your very kind permission and permission from my Senior colleague---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I think my time is being eaten up. Kindly allow me, because the basis of your question has not been---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Just a minute. I have allowed him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. The side of His Excellency (H.E.), the Governor, said that they are going to call four witnesses. We are not sure who those four witnesses are. For purposes of preparation, we just want to know who these four witnesses are, so that we can prepare.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is fair. Can you provide the names of the four witnesses?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I had referenced my volume three. My volume three has my witnesses. The witness coming in is Emanuel Kenga. It is on pay 450 of the same volume that were on with Ms. Museiya.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.speaker_title: The Speaker
entries.text: Why can you not just mention all the four?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The next witness is Kevin Omari Nyabera, and the last one is Douglas Ouma Nyakach. Mr. Kevin Omari Nyabera is my next witness, and the last witness is the one who has sworn an affidavit to which Sen. Orengo alluded to.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: What is the name?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Douglas Ouma Nyakach.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: There is Mr. Kevin and who else? Who is the third one, please?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Emanuel Kenga. Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Senators, on page 450 of the same volume is the affidavit of my next wittiness, that is Mr. Emanuel Kenga. Please, introduce yourself.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The witness for the Governor of Nairobi City County (Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga) took the oath)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Emanuel Kenga. You did swear an affidavit before these proceedings on 13th December 2020. It is located from page 450-527 of volume three.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: That is correct, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You can introduce your field of expertise and experience.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am a document examiner having trained locally and abroad. I retired from the National Police Service (NPS) in the year 2015. I am currently doing private examination on documents. I have an experience of more than 26 years in the field.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Very well. On page 450 is his affidavit. In paragraph seven on page 451, there is a list your expertise. You have been appearing in court cases.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Exactly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: As an expert witness?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: According to your testimony, you received a request to examine the signatures which were purportedly signed by the Members of the County Assembly (MCAs) in the Nairobi City County Assembly, and you came to a finding. Please, explain.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I got a request from Ondieki and Ondieki Advocates requesting me to examine some documents involving handwriting and signatures. I did that as requested and came up with my findings which are contained in my report.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: A copy of the signatures you examined is what was submitted to this hon. Senate by the Speaker of the county assembly. You can confirm that they are located on page 481-894 of volume three. They are contained in your report.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I marked the bundle as (a). There were some documents attached to the bundle. I had to examine the same. There, we have handwritings and signatures. My findings are as follows.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: There is report on page 473, which is tied on the foot of the same page, in which you said that you made a finding thereon that there were several signatures there that has been forged or were not genuine. Do you confirm that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I examined the handwritings on the entries on serial number 1-88. In my opinion, entry number 3, 4, 9 20, 69, 85 were made by the same author.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, in a nutshell, the list that was given by the County Assembly in alleged confirmation of the majority having voted to impeach the Governor contained forgeries.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, there are some writings which were made by an individual and I have mentioned the entries in my report. I also went further and examined the signatures on the lists. In my opinion, the signatures had different similarities, meaning that they were made by different authors.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You confirm the accuracy of your report because you have signed at page 474?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Exactly, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I wish to produce the same report as evidence in this Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much. You will be cross-examined on the same by the other side.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Can I proceed, Mr. Speaker, Sir?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. I am going to ask just a few questions in two minutes and then I will yield to my colleague Mr. Okatch to proceed. Mr. Emmanuel Kenga, you said that you are a qualified forensic document examiner, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emmanuel Kenga
entries.speaker_title: (The Witness for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: And you are a retired commissioner of police?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: That is correct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Have you attached any documents as exhibits of your qualification as a document examiner in the bundle of documents?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I have not attached my training documents as a document examiner but I have the documents with me.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. You said you are a retired commissioner of police.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: That is correct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Are you a retired commissioner of police, or you were fired from the service?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I was not fired.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You said from the very onset that you got a request from the firm of Ondieki & Ondieki Company Advocates, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Correct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Did you get any request to verify any signatures from the Office of the Speaker, Nairobi City County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Did you receive any request from the Clerk?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I received a request from Ondieki & Ondieki Company Advocates.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You can confirm that the firm of Ondieki & Ondieki Company Advocates was not the author of the documents you were given to verify, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Secondly, you said that you did a forensic analysis of the documents that you were given?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I did an examination on the documents which were forwarded. I did as requested and came out with findings which are in my report.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Can you kindly be very specific on which documents were given to you for analysis? Kindly provide us with the name of the document that you were given for analysis and, probably, the page it appears in this bundle of documents. Kindly tell us the document you were given to analyse.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that document is on page 481. The heading is "Requisition of the County Assembly of Nairobi." That is from pages 481 up to 527.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You confirm that the document at page 481 is a communication from the Assembly to the Speaker of this House? So, you were also told to verify the authenticity of that document? Is that what you are testifying?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is a list in between of MCAs from serial Nos.1 to 88.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Which page is that please?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the list of names from serial nos. 1 to 88 is from pages 491 up to 494.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Although it is a bit faint, I presume these are the names of MCAs who may have participated in some activity somewhere because it is a bit faint and I cannot see. Is it true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Yes, these are MCAs who participated. We have names against their signatures.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you so much. Is there any other document that you were given that has their names and signatures?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: These are the documents that I worked on.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You were never given a document for purposes of comparing. There were no other signatures of MCAs that you were supposed to compare with the documents contained from pages 491 to 494. Is it true or not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I never got any signatures from any MCA to compare with whatever I have on pages 491 up to 494.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Then how did you arrive to the conclusion that these signatures were forged if you were not comparing with any other signatures?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: The request was to examine the handwritings on the list, including the signatures appended against the names.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Which other handwritings were you comparing with?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: The hand writings on the list.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Okay, let us go to your report. Can you open where your report is please? You have highlighted that there are particular handwritings that had been forged. Is it true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: That is not true your honour. I have not said there was forgery. I have said I examined the writings on some serial numbers and the names.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Then what was your conclusion?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: My conclusion is that for Serial Nos. 3, 4, 9, 26, 29 and 85, the writing was made by the same author.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: What becomes of the other serial numbers? You need to help the Senate arrive at a conclusion. What is it that you want the Senate to know?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the examination was on the handwritings of the names.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: What about the names? That is what this House needs to know.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: The request I got was to examine the handwritings of the names and whether they were made by different people or the same author. The finding is that for the serial numbers I have given out, according to my opinion, those names were made by the same author. The reason is that I got some peculiar individual characteristics on the writings. I gave a few characteristics on the capital "M", capital "K", 2 and 6. That means that the serial numbers I have mentioned in the report were made by the same author.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Brian Biko Ashioya
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you, very much. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like to end, but with a closing remark that if a distinction has to be made, there must be two documents. My colleague Mr. Okatch will take the stand.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your intervention, Counsel Kinyanjui?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
