entries.text: Thank you, very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Counsel Interjections)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Only one person can speak at a time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: My learned friend who was previously cross-examining my witness asked for two minutes. He has taken 10. That is why the orange light is on because their time is almost up. Therefore, they cannot expand their cross-examination through this added scope.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have just been notified that we have five minutes. I think it is best that we stick to our roles. There is someone keeping the time. I will just take three minutes on one issue. Sir, I will ask you one or two questions. You have indicated that you are retired.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Yes, I retired from the police service.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: In this aspect of yours, you were working from the National Police Service (NPS).

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Exactly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Do you know about a petition that you filed challenging your dismissal from service?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Yes, that was through vetting.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Is it true that you were fired because of producing two contradictory reports?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: That is not true, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I am ready to explain.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: It is not about explaining. Are you saying that is not true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: It is not true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I will refer you to paragraph 25 of that Petition. I will just read it so that it can rest. Is it true or false that you were the second petitioner?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I cannot remember whether I was second because we were four in the Petition.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You are not sure whether you were the second petitioner?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I am not very sure whether I was second, third or fourth.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: The second petitioner goes by your names in this matter. This is what the court said- "The second petitioner responded to the charges denying the allegations and explaining the facts surrounding the two complaints. The second petitioner was vetted on 7th of March, 2014 and a decision dismissing the second petitioner from service was made on the 22nd of May, 2014 on grounds that he exhibited professional negligence in submitting contradicting reports to the court and further that he lacked financial probity for failing to explain how he acquired his assets." Are those words new to you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Those words are in the petition. Allow me to explain. When you ask me another question---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: There is time to explain. I only have two minutes. Are they referring to you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Your time is almost up.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Just one minute.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Those allegations were false that is why I was acquitted. I was to be reinstated, but I had attained the age of 60 years. I went home honourably.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: That is all, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel Harrison, what was your intervention?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: My intervention was that my learned friend was referring to a document which the hon. Members do not have. I think that is an ambush on the House. Allow me now to re- examine in a minute. Mr. Karisa, you can confirm that by virtue of the fact that you have five names with a similar handwriting, therefore, it is only one person in lieu of five who wrote that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: According to my opinion, the writings in the entries I mentioned in my report were made by the same author.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Therefore, instead of the list you have of 88 Members it reduces by 5 to 82. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What were you to examine? If you look at page 471, it is clearly stating that the scope of your investigation was to the 88 names. Could you refer that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: My mandate was to examine that list from Serial No. 1 up to Serial No. 88.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What were you then supposed to do? Read that line. To ascertain whether it was generated by the same person. Is that not the scope of your instruction from Mr. Ondieki?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: My mandate was to ascertain and examine whether the documents were generated by the same persons.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: And you did exactly that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: I did as I was requested.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Lastly, you were told that you were fired from the Department of Police. Therefore, you had 'a', 'b' or 'c' wrong. You have been a professional witness in court cases that have even gone to the Court of Appeal and your document examination been confirmed, affirmed and taken in convicting criminals.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have been in this for the last 27 years. I have given my expert opinion in all courts in here in Kenya. I have been to Dar- es-Salaam and Kampala on the same business. I have done all I can in this police service. I have done my best and I have not had any complaints so far.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Very well. We have copies of some, not all of those because they are too many to bring before the Senate. We have copies of Court of Appeal and High Court decisions convicting criminals even for murder owing to your expertise evidence. Confirm that we have that on page 454-470 in the same Vol. 3.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: That is correct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, your work is professionally recognized.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: Well recognized.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you confirm that the number of MCAs allegedly signing did not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Emanuel Karisa Kenga
entries.text: They were signed by several people in the document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: My time is up. Thank you very much. I can have my next witness, Mr. Speaker, Sir. He is Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach on page 653 of the same volume. As we prepare, I beg that clip produced as Exhibit 13 which we saw yesterday, be played in silence mode as the witness testifies so that we do not interrupt you by again taking too much time on it. The video about the County Assembly delivery of the documents be played as Mr. Nyakach takes to podium.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Witness for the Governor of Nairobi City County (Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach) took oath)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Nyakach, you have sworn an affidavit in furtherance, defending the governor against the accusations of impeachment. The affidavit is found from page 648 to 653 of Volume 3 of the governor's bundle of documents marked D. Do you confirm that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Could you tell this honourable House what you do for a living?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I am a driver in one of the law firms in Nairobi City County; Ondieki & Ondieki Company Advocates, located in Corner House, third floor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Now, the events of 3rd December, 2020 are recorded in your affidavit in detail and you say that you went to Nairobi City County Assembly on that day at 2.00 p.m. Do you confirm that you have said that in paragraph two?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you also confirm that you were in the company of Mr. Ondieki and Madam Cecilia Naliaka and Mr. Moses Okerosi on that day? What had you go to do?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as a driver, I was instructed by my boss to stand by. I did not ask the reason why because as a driver, you do not need to ask so many questions. Later, I was instructed that by 2 p.m. we were supposed to take documents to Nairobi City County Assembly to the Speaker of the City County Assembly at City Hall. I was ready to do so as a driver.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Now, the events of what transpired were captured in a video. After you arrived at the Assembly, would you confirm that, that is what you have testified about in paragraph Nos.5, 6, 7 and 9? Hon. Members, I will refer you to the same Volume, paragraph Nos.5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, all the way to 25 of the affidavit.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir. It is true and it was more serious than that. You can even see me there standing adjacent to my boss, Mr. Ondieki, the lawyer.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Could the clip just go a little bit back where someone is flushing their hand?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The clip was replayed)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir, that man walked almost 120 metres thrice as if he was---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Is that you? Pause right there.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The video clip was paused)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Is that you in a brown, cream-ish suit?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is me standing there in a suit and a mask.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Laughter)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I was standing there overseeing the circles. It was more serious. It was like I was not in Kenya. It was unprofessional.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Okay. Let us save time. Now that event you are witnessing, was the County Assembly gate accessible?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: The main entrance was only for the Members of the County Assembly (MCAs). It is because at that gate, there was someone wearing a coat, the same as those of the City Council workers.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Keep playing the video. Yes, go ahead.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The video was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, that is me. Inside, there were police men and we were outside. It was terrible.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What are the documents we can see over there with you and Mr. Ondieki?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, those are documents I was ordered to carry. They are now being unloaded.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Can we see you behind there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I am standing there. That is my job as the driver.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Okay, the documents are being offloaded?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, they are being offloaded from the vehicle by that person who is walking in and out---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Of the County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, the County Assembly. It was about two to three hours. It is a short man, a little fat and not slender like me.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Did you witness Mr. Ondieki being given access?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: It was not easy. Mr. Ondieki was denied access. He even said, "I am very sorry. I am a lawyer." Mr. Ondieki was shouting. "I am a lawyer, why deny me entry and that is my job. I can serve anywhere in Kenya or the world because I am a lawyer." It was terrible.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: To your knowledge, he was going to do what at the County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: He was going to serve the Speaker of the County Assembly as required by law because he was aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: We can see there Mr. Ondieki is holding the documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Ondieki is arguing with somebody. He is that short man from the Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Very well. That is the event you have narrated about on the 3rd December, 2020. You have captured the time in Paragraph 5 to be a few minutes to 2.00 p.m. At what time did you leave? Before I come to that, in Paragraph 22, Page 651, you say something there. You were there and what happens eventually?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I was there after a long argument. There was a police officer. There is a difference between a police officer and an administration officer. Those are two different things. There were about seven administration officers. I heard them say: "Kwani ni nini, wacha tu apeane. Muache tu apeane." That is in Kiswahili.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What do you understand to " apeane ."?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: " Wacha apeane documents." 'Just give him a chance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Did you see the documents enter into the Nairobi City County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: No, still it was chaotic. It was as if it was war.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, we can conclude that the document that you had there. On page 535, this is a copy of the document you had gone to deliver with Mr. Ondieki? I just want to address the witness and show him. It runs all the way to page 572. Is that part of the document that we saw you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: It is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The document running from page 535 to 572. Is that part of the documents you took?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is it. Your last remark on what you witnessed and what we have seen on that clip. What would you say?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I have seen the documents outside the entrance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: No, just about that event. What transpired?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: What transpired was terrible. Ours was very simple. It was just to deliver the documents inside there for about two to five minutes, for them to be stamped as required by law. I wondered as a driver. As you know, in Nairobi if you are canning your child, people come very first as if there is a tug of war. What I saw there was not professional. It was as if we are not in this country where there is law and order, and people follow the law. There was no law there from inside the Speaker's office because he was the one who ordered us not to present those papers. I have one.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What time did you leave? My time is up.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I need even six minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: No. What time did you leave?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: We stayed for more than three hours like statues.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you. Mr. Speaker, Sir. I will rest at that point. You will be asked questions now by the lawyers of the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I am ready to answer.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach, confirm to this particular honourable House whether you are a court process server.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I am a driver.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Just confirm whether you are a court process server.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you so much. Your duty is actually just to drive the boss.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: My duty is to drive and if there is any luggage that I am supposed to deliver, it is 100 per cent that I am granted to remove from the trunk to where it is supposed to be delivered.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. You have confirmed that on that particular day you were driving Mr. Evans Ondieki to the premises of the Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Not Mr. Evans Ondieki only. We were with some lawyers; Ms. Naliaka, Mr. Ekorosi and I. I was driving people and not a person.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: In the video that you have shown us, confirm that you have said that, that was Mr. Ondieki. Do you confirm? Just answer 'Yes' or 'No.'

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. Do you know that Mr. Ondieki has not deponed any affidavit confirming the events that you have indicated today?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Being a driver, mine is to carry the luggage. To confirm what was inside the documents was not my job.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: That is okay. Just listen to my question. Is it within your knowledge whether or not Mr. Ondieki, as you were doing this affidavit, whether your boss, whom you were with, also filed or signed an affidavit confirming the said facts that you have told us?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Signed inside or at the Assembly? They are two different things. Signed in his office or inside the Speaker's office?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Where did you sign this particular statement that appears on Page 652?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I was the one who signed it. It was not at the Speaker's office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Where did you sign it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I can sign that one in the law firm or any place.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Where did you sign it? The question is where.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: In the office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Which office? Your office, I believe? Kindly, answer my question. You signed this particular affidavit on Page 652.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Kindly advise us whether you can remember where you signed this affidavit.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I signed it at Mr. Ondieki's office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Was Mr. Ondieki aware that you were signing this affidavit?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. You have indicated that there should be law and order. Is that true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, it is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: On that particular day, do you know what was to happen at the County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I did not know. Mine was to deliver and unload as a driver.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: That is okay. Did you know whether Mr. Ondieki had any invitation to appear there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: That one was not my job to know.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You do not know. Do you know that for you to appear, you had to give prior notice to the Clerk of that particular Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: As a driver, I cannot know that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: The only thing you know is that a lawyer can enter any premises at any time because he is a lawyer.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, if he is a professional lawyer. We have court servers who are trained to serve anybody. As a lawyer, that is his work from which he gets his daily bread. That is what I know.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Therefore, all lawyers in this country can come to these particular proceedings today and no one should stop them.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Ondieki was not mad to deliver these huge documents to the Speaker without instructions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: In your document, show us the instructions that Mr. Ondieki had to appear on behalf of the Governor on the third day.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Mr. Ondieki appeared for the Governor just like any other lawyer in the world. He was picked by the Governor to appear on his behalf.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I have asked you a very straight forward question. Do you have any letter by the Governor saying that Mr. Ondieki will appear on the 3rd of December, 2020 on my behalf? Do you have it or have you seen it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I do not know. That is not my work to know.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Have you ever seen such a document?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: That is not my job. My job is to deliver the documents as instructed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Do you know that on this particular day, the Governor had been invited to appear virtually? Was it within your knowledge?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Mr. Ondieki can answer that, but not me as a driver.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You have told us that you appeared in a brown suit on that day. Confirm that your face was not visible in that video.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: You can see me. I am slender and tall. Mr. Speaker, Sir, can it be replayed?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: No. We saw you in your suit.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: If you were not keen, you could not see me properly. If your eyes cannot see, you can use glasses. I can offer to take you there one day.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: On this particular video that we have, does it tell us the date that this video was taken?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: The date in the world, learned person---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Just answer the question, does it tell us the date?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, protect me from harassment. I need protection from the counsel. He is harassing me.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: You are protected.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you gave a direction yesterday that there can be a 'yes' or 'no' answer. The same should apply to save my time. That is the only issue I am concerned with.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Your time is almost up.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Because of that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: It is actually up.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. On this particular video, you are the one who took that video?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Hon. Senators come from different areas and constituencies. My work was specifically different and assigned by my boss. I know the person who took the video, but it was not my work to take the video. We were all there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. Confirm to me as I finish the documents that you were taking? Is there anywhere in that particular video that you have demonstrated that these are the documents that you were taking?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir. It was demonstrated very well. They are there. You can see my car. I was there. What next?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: To that particular extent, you have indicated that the Speaker of the Assembly denied you access. What proof do you have for that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: I have said and I will repeat in this honourable Senate, we were denied access. "We", I was not alone.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order. Counsel, your time is up.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. One question. Mr. Douglas, in paragraph three of your affidavit, did you read it before you signed? It says: "On the midmorning of the 3rd December, 2020, Mr. Evans Ondieki, Advocate, had informed me that he would require me to be on standby to drive him, Mr. Aliaka, advocate, and Mr. Moses to represent His Excellency hon. Mike Sonko Mbuvi during the proceedings on the said date slated at 2.30 p.m."

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is what you know you had gone to do on that day.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much. Asante. Mr. Speaker, Sir, my fourth witness is Mr. Newton Munene in Volume IV, marked D.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir, enjoy your holiday.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Laughter)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Thank you. Counsel, is Mr. Newton Munene one of the witnesses you said you will call?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Yes. Then I will call the Governor. I had said out of the other seven I was to call---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: You said you will call four witnesses.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I had said four and then I call the Governor. I said so. This is the last other witness then I call the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, if I may, the witnesses that we were told were to be called were Mr. Douglas Ouma Nyakach, hon. Silvia Museiya and Mr. Kevin Omari Nyabera.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I am sorry. I read the wrong name. I apologize. It was Mr. Newton Munene.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, if I may, it will only be fair that we know who is coming. Where is the document in question for the Senators to follow? Abrupt wake up and telling us this witness is also confusing the Senate to follow. Kindly, let us be candid and practice fair as referee. This House should be an arbiter.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What you gave us was Mr. Kevin Omari Nyabera. What has happened?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The name of my last witness was to be Mr. Newton Munene Njiru. I read the wrong page. I confused that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this will be harassing the County Government and this House. Let us stick to what we speak to. If that is not what he stated, let him withdraw that witness, let him present His Excellency the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like to clarify because this witness had produced this way back in time. The issue has arisen because I had original seven witnesses. When I called out that name from our original list, in that step, I had mix up. I apologize. There is prejudice.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, we cannot allow that. You either produce Mr. Kevin Omari Nyabera or you step him down and call His Excellency the Governor. We cannot keep taking the House forth and backwards. Produce Mr. Kevin Omari Nyabera, step him down and produce His Excellency the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I will call Mr. Kevin Omari Nyabera. That is okay.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, for purposes of preparing for the next witness, Mr. Kinyanjui might want to tell us the document he is relying on so that we can prepare.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Volume 3. The certificate for production of the video we have just seen and the photographic evidence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I did not get the description clearly from Mr. Kinyanjui as marked by the Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Volume 3, audit 2 on page 644.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Is that okay? Proceed now.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, so that he save time, I could request that we have that video clip playing so that we can close on that aspect of the evidence.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Video clip was played)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: [The Witness for the Governor of Nairobi City County (Mr. Kelvin OMari Nyabera) took oath]

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Please, tell the court what you do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: I am the personal assistant to Evans Ondieki, the lawyer who is representing the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: There is that clip that we have seen. Would you confirm that what the events we are seeing recorded therein reflect the events you witnessed?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Would you confirm that those are the events of which date?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: They refer to 3rd December 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Would you confirm the time?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: 2 p.m.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Between 2:00 p.m and what time?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What place was that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: This was at the door outside the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The entrance to the Nairobi County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, you were able then to take those images.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes. I took those images.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you confirm that that is the video clip?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: And the certificate, which you produced at page 644 and page 645 of volume 3, is reflective of that accurate recording?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Would you like that to be admitted as evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: My last question. Since you state there that you had the events of the 3rd December 2020, were you in any way induced to take that video recording?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A Video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: No, I was not induced in any matters regarding to this taking of the pictures because we came out of the office from our daily duties. We went with the lawyer to the Assembly where I took the office phone and took the pictures of what was happening at the door of the county assembly because there was commotion. So, I took those photos and videos personally using the office phone.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much. Did you say the office phone? Did I hear you right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: I said Ondieki and Ondieki's Office phone.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You are an employee at Ondieki and Ondieki?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes. I am the personal assistant.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you. Your purpose of that visit was to present the documents?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: My purpose of the visit was to go with Evans Ondieki who is my employer, to the designated meeting point because my work duty is to help Evans Ondieki in his daily to day in day out duties.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: So, you only duty in that place was to take photos and that was all?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: No. We carried documents from the office, which were going to be presented to the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kevin Kokebe
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I do not have further question. I will probably give my learned senior, Mr. Ndegwa to conclude.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I have only one question. You certified this video in what capacity, in terms of the taking of the video? Limit yourself to the video itself. What capacity?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Come again.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Other than the Personal Assistant to Mr. Ondieki, what other capacity did you take in terms of your qualifications for photos or photography?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: I took those photos because during the presentation of documents at the County Assembly there was commotion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Address the professionalism in issues of photography. Limit yourself to that. Are you a professional photographer? Are you trained?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: I am not trained to perform those works, but I took the photos.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: What was the magnification of the camera that you used?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: The phone I used---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: The magnification for purposes of clarity because that video is not clear to us. The magnification, address the question of the specifications of the camera that you used.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Let me explain.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: You do not know. Finally, you say that you edited this through a desktop. Correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Which desktop was that, where was it and who is the owner?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Kelvin Omari Nyabera
entries.text: The office desktop.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Okay, no further questions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I do not have any further questions to this witness. I will now call his Excellency the Governor to testify. I would like to yield to my learned friend, Mr. Nyamu, as he takes up the evidence after which I will then resume thereafter as we proceed. Mr. Speaker, Sir, if I may get your direction. So far, what is my time bank? We do not want to offend you, Mr. Speaker, Sir, and Hon. Members. I would like to operate within the timeline.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I will tell you in a short while.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will be patient.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: You have two hours and thirty-five minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as I indicated, I will yield the time to Mr. Nyamu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: We shall break for lunch at 1.00 p.m. Then resume so that we keep our program. Proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Hon. Members of the Senate, I will lead evidence of His Excellency the Governor. I do not know the issue my learned friend has.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Only one issue--

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Hold on. There is a point of order from, Sen. Wambua.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Enoch Kiio Wambua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we are trying to follow these proceedings. It cannot be that a counsel will decide to address the House through you without your permission. The counsel on the Floor is Mr. Nyamu. If there is another counsel who wants to address the House through you, they should seek your permission.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is true. Proceed Mr. Nyamu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, much obliged and Hon. Member for Kitui. The documents we shall initially use are the documents marked 10E which I believe Hon. Members have. This is the document that bears response to allegations made in the Motion. It has documents filed with it. The other document we are going to use is the document marked 10H. I believe this document that the County Assembly have issues with, they have been resolved so that we may use it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Those are the ones I allowed yesterday?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Yes, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: There is an intervention by Sen. Madzayo.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Stewart Mwachiru Shadrack Madzayo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it looks like we do not have 10H with us. Document 10E and 10G. If 10H can be availed to us, it will be much better.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Check if the documents are present. Those who do not have you can give them. There is an intervention from counsel. Let us hear him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I do not want to ask for directions from this hon. House again. Our understanding when we raised this issue in the morning was that the documents he is now referring to were locked out as documents that were lately filed. Mr. Speaker, Sir, you might want to refresh my memory on your ruling because that is the understanding of the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I allowed them yesterday. Let us proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I knew that was the issue and that is why I sought clarification before he stood. As I indicated, those are the documents that we are going to use initially.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your point of intervention? Let us minimize interruptions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Sen. (Dr.) Ali
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, please allow me. We have been told severally that this is a court. Hon. Members are interfering from every side. Can the Members wait for their time? They are complaining when one of lawyers talk, when another speaks, this is not right. Let us wait.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.speaker_title: The Speaker
entries.text: Order! Order! I think our sugar levels are beginning to go down, but we will address it soon. Counsel, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, at this juncture, with your permission I will ask His Excellency the Governor for Nairobi to take the stand.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Governor of Nairobi City County (Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko) took the oath)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir and Hon. Members, in our evidence we are going to move step by step, charge by charge for ease of proceedings. Your Excellency, you have been charged in the impeachment proceedings with violation of laws, gross misconduct, abuse of office and crimes under national law. On the first charge, you are charged with gross violation of the Constitution and other laws. In 1(a) it is alleged that as governor of Nairobi you have violated Article 201 (a), (b) and (e) of the Constitution on the Principal of Public Finance Management and Section 154 of the Public Finance Management Act. It is alleged that the County Allocation of Revenue Act has also been violated on the use of conditional grants from the national Government by diversion or negligently causing to be diverted funds. For instance, on the use of Roads Levy and bursary funds to pay for garbage collection and lawyers contrary to bursary funds regulations and the approved budget. While you requested for Kshs297 million for bursaries from the Controller of Budget the funds were illegally used to pay garbage contractors and lawyers. Your excellency, what would be your response to that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir and the hon. Members. In the essence of time, I wish to go directly to my responses. I will refer the House to my affidavit on Pages 167 to 172.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is the document marker 10 (h), Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, on page 167 we have a voucher drawn in favour of Nairobi County Bursary Account 2019, being the payment of transfer of bursary funds totaling to Kshs297,500,000. I think this is the Financial Year 2019/2020. In the previous year, 2018/2019, we also allocated the same amount of Kshs297,500,000. The voucher is self-explanatory. It is not stamped 'paid.' All vouchers prepared for payment are stamped 'paid' when the process is complete. So, it is true that this amount was never paid. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will again refer the House to Page 168 of the Vote Account No.R5318 on Nairobi City Education. This is the Bursary Vote Account. It is highlighted and marked that the Kshs297, 500, 000 for the Financial Year 2018/2019 as at the period of July 2019 to June 2020, this amount was availed for the payment of bursary. On page 169 of my annexures in the affidavit, we have the Authority to Incur Expenditure of Kshs297,500,000 for bursary funds. The letter is also self-explanatory. In the last paragraph, the purpose of this memorandum is to request the money to be transferred to the Bursary Fund Account. Mr. Speaker, Sir, on Page 170 the Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) payment from the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) is also a self-explanatory document. These funds were not released and they were intact towards the end of the Financial Year. That is in the last box on stock reason on the end of the financial year. During the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) period, there were so many challenges. Schools were closed. This document is a clear confirmation that the Mover of my Impeachment Motion is dramatizing the entire process. He is playing politics and doing character assassination, because the transaction reference number in Box one is clearly marked and indicated. The processing reference is there. The letter Ref. No.619 is there. This is the CBK; the amount of Kshs297,500,000. The CBK stopped RTGS payments. The bank code and the account number are there. The name of the county holder is Nairobi City County. Mr. Speaker, Sir, the status stopped. The date is 1st September, 2020. They say that we spent this money during the financial year. This is towards the end of the financial year. The CBK confirms that these funds are intact and were transferred back to the CBK account. They are very intact. What the Mover is not telling us--- He said that I refused to release the cheques of the students who used to benefit from my predecessor. However, he is not telling the House what the reason behind my actions was. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will now refer the House to Page 221-360 of my affidavit. Before I move there, I wish to clarify something. I want the Information and Communication (ICT) department to play the clip on bursary release of Kshs297,500,000 for the previous Financial Year. Can we have that clip, please?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: I think you can stop there in the essence of time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Could you give the background of that particular video, your Excellency?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have over a thousand beneficiaries for bursaries disbursed to various beneficiaries in schools countrywide. However, because of time, we cannot play the entire clip.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: When was this documentary taken?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: This documentary was taken and aired in various media stations about six months ago.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In relation to bursary, would you like to state anything in terms of your relationship with the MCAs?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: Yes, but before I go to that, I wish to mention about a document, which I will not table, but for the sake of the HANSARD. This is a certified bank account statement from Co-operative Bank showing that funds amounting to Kshs297,500,000 were transferring from the County Revenue Fund (CRF) Account to Co-operative Bank Account in the FY 2018/2019. It clearly explains and shows all the beneficiaries; that is, the schools and the students. Since we were denied a chance of producing this document, I will just talk about it. We have 80 copies as advised by the Office of the Clerk. Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Mover of the Motion was trying to divert from the real issues. He said that there are cheques that I refused to release. It is true that there are cheques we refused to release because there are some MCAs who opened a fake educational institution at River Road. That has been happening since 2019. It started during my predecessor's time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Which year did you say?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: From 2013 to 2017 when my predecessor was in office. I unearthed that scandal in 2018. It is a sad story. The directors of the fake school are wives and relatives of MCAs. They even get cheques from the National Government-Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) from various constituencies countrywide and also in Nairobi. To prove those allegations, on page 221, we have a memo---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is page 221 of 10(h).

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: We have a self-explanatory memo from an officer from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) at the county offices. That is superintended Eunice Maingi. The letter is self- explanatory. I will quickly go through it in the essence of time. The memo was addressed to me after I complained to the DCI that we needed to investigate Kobudho Education Centre. The memo is dated 7th December, 2018. The Reference number is 11A/2/4/5/VOL.3(99) 2018. A police file was opened by the DCI. The police file number is 111548/2018 and there is a court file because the suspects were arrested and arraigned in court and that matter is ongoing.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What is the document on page 221?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: The court case file is 1992/2018, giving details of the offence. It is about forgery of official documents contrary to Section 345 as read with Section 349 of the Penal Code. Accused are Job Omondi Mark Imboko and three others. I will not read the entire letter. Paragraph 2 says- "During the month of September, 2018, information was received to this office that there is a Community-based Organisation operating in the name and style of Kobudho Education Centre. It was defrauding the County Government by forging bursary cheques. Investigations commenced and the investigators obtained court warrants to investigate the accounts of the community-based organisation housed at Co-operative Bank of Kenya Limited and the County Government Development Account housed at Co-operative Bank, City Hall Branch. In the course of investigations, we establish that the directors of Kobudho Education Centre are as follows- 1. Job Mark Omondi Imboko - This is a county government staff I inherited from the previous administration working under the Department of Water. 2. Francis Odhiambo Ouma - A Personal Assistant (PA) to the MCA who is the ODM Chair for Karen. 3. Quinster Adhiambo Ouma - Wife to the PA of the MCA. 4. Nancy Nasimiyu - Wife to the first accused." This is from the DCI and not Sonko. "In the course of investigations, we established that Francis Ouma is the PA of the MCA for Karen. Investigations were extended to both Co-operative Bank of Kenya and Equity Bank and we obtained original cheques, image cheques, account opening documents for Nairobi County Government and those of the suspects. In Equity Bank, we obtained 77 original cheques; the ones the Mover complained why I have not released them. The cheques were drawn by Nairobi City County Government. Looking at them critically, they were all forged. I will come to that. In Co-operative Bank, we obtained 129 image cheques drawn in favour of this fake school, which does not exist called Kobudho Education Centre. Investigators further established that suspects obtained money from the County Government up to the tune of Kshs4.5 million." Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will just go to the main points in the essence of time. After establishing the identity of the suspects, we involved the services of criminal intelligence personnel from DCI Headquarters. On the fifth day of October, at 3.00 a.m., we apprehended the accused persons. We conducted searches in their houses and recovered 67 original cheques drawn in favour of different schools within the county, 113 bursary application forms in the names of different applicants within Karen Ward and two payment vouchers originating from Nairobi City County Government. Mr. Speaker, Sir, after investigations the suspects were charged. The handwriting and specimen signatures of the four suspects were taken and forwarded to the document examiner at the Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) headquarters to ascertain whether the accused persons were the authors of the cheques. We are yet to receive the report. These are some of the witnesses. The Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officers wanted to bring them to testify, but in the interest of time the report is here. Authenticated suspects and court charge sheets are there. Since this is a very important memo, let me just finish because I am on the last paragraph. The suspects - the relatives of MCAs - were arraigned in court on 8th October, 2018 and pleaded not guilty to all the charges. They were released on a cash bail of Ksh400,000 or alternative surety of Kshs500,000. The case was marked for mention at Milimani Law Court No.5 on 5th January, 2019, with a view of fixing a hearing date, which was fixed. Mr. Speaker, Sir, the DCI is putting a note in my memo of 7th December, 2018. She said- "The case requires travelling because we have witnesses in Homa Bay County and some areas of Rift Valley. Therefore, we require urgent facilitation to enable us move with speed and cover what is remaining before the hearing date." Moving to the next page 233, these proxies of MCAs were charged, as I said before. The case Police file Number is 11/54H/2018. Details of the suspects are there. The relatives of MCAs are there with their description, gender and tribe; Male, Luo; Female, Luhya. The offences are self-explanatory. (1) Conspiracy to defraud contrary to Section 317 of the Penal Code.

entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu

entries.text: Number two.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Mbuvi Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: Let me first go to the details of the charges.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Perhaps, Your Excellency, in the interest of time, we would wish to refer to the document appearing on Page 223, all the way to 228. What document is that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: From page 223 to 226 are various charges which were preferred.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What document is that appearing on page---.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Governor of Nairobi City
entries.text: County (Hon. Mike Sonko): Charge sheets with so many counts.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: There are other documents referred to at Page 227 and 228.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Governor of Nairobi City
entries.text: County (Hon. Mike Sonko): I think before go there, I have a pertinent message to raise.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Carry on.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: These the details of the charges. We already have the names of the accused. On diverse dates between 30th May, 2016--- Before I became Governor of Nairobi City County Government, this scandal was there. Taxpayers' money was being swindled in Nairobi City County Government. On diverse dates between 30th May, 2016, during my predecessor's time, and 13th September my first month in office in 2017, meaning that I was the one who stopped the scandal during my time. It was ongoing and we were losing government funds during the last administration's time. Between 30th May, 2016 and 13th September, 2017 at an unknown place within the Republic of Kenya, jointly with others not before court--- There were even some MCAs who were supposed to be charged with these suspects--- I do not know why to date they have not been arrested. We have current MCA and 10 more who have not been arrested and charged, due to political interference. I proceed with details of the charges. It reads- "Jointly with others not before court by deceit and fraudulent means conspired to defraud Nairobi City County Government a sum of Ksh3,225,000 by forging bursary cheques, purporting them to have been issued by Mr. Ekaya Almasi who was our Chief Officer for Finance and Martha Wambugu an accountant working with the Nairobi City County Government, a fact you knew to be false." That is Count No. 1. I will not go to all the counts, but all these offences started during the previous administration's time. However, I think there are some important details; maybe Members will read for themselves. They were charged with eight counts according to Page 226-228. Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is also another count, which is No. 9. Some charges are extremely important to this case. Since yesterday there were some grievous allegations, which were made by the mover of this motion, you will also allow me to do a clarification on the scandal by MCAs who were diverting public funds for poor students, to benefit themselves and their wives and families. Allow me to do a clarification because after banking these cheques to their fake school, they used to withdraw the money in cash from various bank branches in Nairobi City County. There are some charges where these proxies, who are wives of MCAs, used to withdraw this money. I think I will find it in one of the counts which are here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Look at Page 234 of that document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Mike Sonko
entries.speaker_title: (The Governor of Nairobi City County)
entries.text: There is a bank Statement, but I wanted first that we move systematically, page by page as we reach there because we want to prove our case belong reasonable doubt. Mr. Speaker, Sir, on page 227 are cheque numbers of the diverted cheques which were drawn by the County, diverted and banked to this Kobudho Educational Centre account. Since this scandal involved various bank withdrawals and we needed to save the county from being swindled of bursary fund, we had to involve the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK). We have a DCI department at the CBK. I refer the House to Page 229, where we have a letter from Banking Fraud Investigations Department; Ref: DCI/BFI/SEC/4/ 4. Vol. 308/ 25, dated 14th August, 2018. The letter is addressed to us, County Secretary, County Government of Nairobi and attention to the Chief Officer for Finance and Chief Officer, Legal Department; Ref. BFID, Inquiry Number 479 of 2018. It says- "Suspected fraud in respect of this fake school, Kobudho Educational Centre, which was opened by MCAs purposely to divert bursary funds to benefit themselves." This was ongoing from the previous administration. I do not want to repeat myself. I stopped this scandal. Mr. Speaker, Sir, the letter is self-explanatory. The members of the public do not have this document. You will just allow me to take the public through this document. "This office is investigating a fraud case where the above institution through its Equity Bank Account No.1250168255007 was issued with multiple Nairobi City County Government development cheques, which were later cleared and paid through the above quoted account. To enable us complete our investigations, please, furnish us with the following, of which we did- (i) official list of bursary applications and beneficiaries for the period between May 2016 - before I became the Governor of Nairobi City County - 2017 and July 2018; (ii) certified copies of counter files for the cheque numbers as per the attached account statement; (iii)an officer whose duty is to disburse the funds to record statement to the effect; and, (iv) any other information that can assist the investigations. Thanking you for your continued support." The letter is signed by Mr. Tobias Obondi for Director, Banking Fraud Investigation Department. Mr. Speaker, Sir, Page 231 is also a summary of investigations. There are various letters written to various schools. For instance, the Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI), there is a letter she wrote to Mulinge High School. It was on investigation on theft of bursary funds of Nairobi City County Government. "This office is investigating a case of theft. It is alleged that some officers of Nairobi City County Government in conspiracy with other members of the public stole funds meant for bursary allocation issued by the Nairobi City County Government. It is on record that some students in those schools are beneficiaries of the said bursary allocations. This is, therefore, to request you that you grant the bearers of this letter corporation in their investigation." It is signed by Eunice Maingi. Mr. Speaker, Sir, at this stage, I wish the ICT department to play the clip because the story was in the public domain. Before I go there, there is a response from the Principal of this school. He has signed to it as reference Nairobi City County bursary cheque purported for Mulinge High School. It says- "The above matter refers. Kindly, note that the school did not receive the said cheque." Secondly, the name indicated is not the name of the school. Thirdly, the school has not had any student by the name indicated." It is signed by the school. At this juncture, I request the ICT to play. The scandal was in the public domain when we were unearthing it. Can you play that Citizen TV clip?
